progressiveGuide.title: Simple present versus ongoing action
progressiveGuide.pattern: habitual: verb + නවා · ongoing: verb + මින් ඉන්නවා
progressiveGuide.description: The -නවා form is the regular or habitual present. Use -මින් ඉන්නවා when you want to emphasize that the action is happening right now.

examples.en: He/she eats rice every day.
He/she is eating rice now.

rules.title: Infinitive to Present / Nonpast
rules.description: Standard conversion of the infinitive form ending in -anna/inna/enna to the present or habitual nonpast -anava/inava/enava. This is not a dedicated English-style continuous form; use a -මින් ඉන්නවා construction to make an ongoing action explicit.

rules.title: Conjunctive Participle Formation
rules.description: Formation of the 'having done' or 'after doing' form, often ending in -la or -illa.
rules.note: Irregular roots like ya- (to go) change significantly to gihilla.

rules.title: Past Tense Regular Transformation
rules.description: Most past tense forms involve changing the root vowel (e.g., a - e) and appending a suffix like -uva, -a, or -una.

rules.title: Intransitive/Passive marker -enava
rules.description: Verbs ending in -enava typically indicate an involuntary action, passive state, or motion, and often take a past tense ending in -una.

forms.label: Infinitive
forms.function: Use before helpers such as ඕනේ, ආසයි, and පුළුවන්.

examples.en: I want/need to read a book.
He/she likes to read a book.

forms.label: Present / nonpast
forms.function: Use for simple present, habitual, or contextually future actions; use -මින් ඉන්නවා to make an action explicitly ongoing.

examples.en: I read a book every day.
He/she reads a book now.
We read a book.

forms.label: Past
forms.function: Use for a completed action.

examples.en: I did read a book yesterday.
He/she did read a book.
We did read a book.

forms.label: Conjunctive participle
forms.function: Use to link this action to the next one or to show it as completed.

examples.en: I have finished reading a book.
He/she went after reading a book.
He/she has completed reading a book.

referenceLessons.title: Sinhala verbs 81-100
referenceLessons.goal: Study 20 Sinhala verbs, their main forms, and preserved romanized alternatives.

grammarLessons.title: Present and regular actions with -නවා
grammarLessons.explanation: The common colloquial -නවා form covers present, habitual, and contextually future actions.

examples.en: I study Sinhala every day.
He or she drinks coffee in the morning.
We play cricket on weekends.
I drink water in the morning.
You work on Saturdays.
He or she walks in the evening.
We listen to Sinhala every day.
She cooks twice a week.
They play after school.

grammarLessons.title: Completed past events
grammarLessons.pattern: past verb form at the end
grammarLessons.explanation: Past forms vary by verb, so learn frequent forms such as ගියා, ආවා, කළා, දැක්කා, and කිව්වා as whole units.

examples.en: We went to Colombo yesterday.
She made breakfast.
I spoke to him yesterday.
I woke up early this morning.
You read well yesterday.
He or she came by bus.
We ate dinner at night.
She wrote a letter to her friend.
They arrived on time.

grammarLessons.title: Infinitives ending in -න්න
grammarLessons.explanation: The -න්න form expresses to do and combines with wants, ability, purpose, and other verbs.

examples.en: I want to speak Sinhala.
We need to leave early.
She went to the shop to buy the book.
I want to stay a little longer.
We need to understand this.
He or she went to the shop to buy bread.
She tried to fall asleep quickly.

examples.si: ඔවුන් ගමන පටන් ගන්න ලෑස්ති වුණා.
examples.en: They got ready to start the trip.
Can you read this?

grammarLessons.title: Chaining actions with -ලා
grammarLessons.explanation: A -ලා participle connects a completed action to the next event.

examples.en: I ate and went home.
He or she opened the door and went inside.

examples.si: මම තේ හදලා වැඩ පටන් ගත්තා.
examples.en: I made tea and started work.
I washed my hands and ate.

examples.si: එයා බෑග් එක අරගෙන පිටත් වුණා.
examples.en: He or she took the bag and left.
We closed the door and slept.

examples.si: ඇය කවුළුව ඇරලා පිට බලලා හිටියා.
examples.en: She opened the window and looked outside.

progressiveGuide.title: Simple present versus ongoing action
progressiveGuide.pattern: habitual: verb + නවා · ongoing: verb + මින් ඉන්නවා
progressiveGuide.description: The -නවා form is the regular or habitual present. Use -මින් ඉන්නවා when you want to emphasize that the action is happening right now.

examples.en: He/she eats rice every day.
He/she is eating rice now.

rules.title: Infinitive to Present / Nonpast
rules.description: Standard conversion of the infinitive form ending in -anna/inna/enna to the present or habitual nonpast -anava/inava/enava. This is not a dedicated English-style continuous form; use a -මින් ඉන්නවා construction to make an ongoing action explicit.

rules.title: Conjunctive Participle Formation
rules.description: Formation of the 'having done' or 'after doing' form, often ending in -la or -illa.
rules.note: Irregular roots like ya- (to go) change significantly to gihilla.

rules.title: Past Tense Regular Transformation
rules.description: Most past tense forms involve changing the root vowel (e.g., a - e) and appending a suffix like -uva, -a, or -una.

rules.title: Intransitive/Passive marker -enava
rules.description: Verbs ending in -enava typically indicate an involuntary action, passive state, or motion, and often take a past tense ending in -una.

levels.title: Basic
levels.description: Short stories, core words, pronouns, simple past events, and basic sentence order.
levels.readiness: Finish 4 lessons with at least 70% practice accuracy.

levels.title: Foundation
levels.description: Needs, wants, negation, case endings, and common story connectors.
levels.readiness: Finish 6 more lessons and feel comfortable identifying final verbs.

levels.title: Story
levels.description: Longer scenes, dialogue, reported thought with කියලා, and paragraph-level meaning.
levels.readiness: Finish 8 story lessons and shadow lines without stopping every word.

levels.title: Conversation
levels.description: Speaker turns, questions, responses, casual phrasing, and faster listening.
levels.readiness: Finish 8 dialogue-heavy lessons and respond in short Sinhala.

levels.title: Advanced
levels.description: Podcast and real-speech material with slang, unclear audio, and less controlled context.
levels.readiness: Use freely once you can follow the topic without translating every word.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 1
courseLessons.focus: Core words and simple sentence order
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Recognize a first set of letters and notice short versus long vowels and dental versus retroflex sounds.

grammarLessons.title: Indefinite singular nouns with -ක් / -ෙක්
grammarLessons.explanation: A singular noun meaning a or one commonly carries an indefinite ending. The exact form depends on the noun and whether it is animate.

examples.en: I have a book.
There is a dog outside.
She got a tea.

grammarLessons.title: Adjectives come before nouns
grammarLessons.explanation: A descriptive adjective normally appears before the noun and does not change for gender or number in ordinary spoken Sinhala.

examples.en: I want the red shirt.
That is a big house.
These are new books.

grammarLessons.title: Default subject-object-verb order
grammarLessons.explanation: A neutral Sinhala sentence normally places the main verb last.

examples.en: I read the book.
I drink tea.
She writes a letter.
I drink coffee.
We listen to songs.
You make food.
He or she opens the door.
She starts the class.
They hit the ball.

grammarLessons.title: Time and place before the verb
grammarLessons.explanation: Time and place information usually arrives before the final action.

examples.en: I am going home today.
We are going to school tomorrow.
He or she goes to the shop in the morning.
I am going to the shop today.
We are going to the beach tomorrow.
He or she is staying home tonight.
She goes to the office in the morning.
They go to the temple in the evening.
You are going to class now.

courseLessons.focus: Core words and simple sentence order
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Open and close a short friendly interaction politely.

grammarLessons.title: Adjective descriptions
grammarLessons.explanation: Many descriptions work as complete predicates without an extra copula.

examples.en: This food is tasty.
The weather is good today.
That room is big.
This tea is tasty.
Today is quiet.
That story is long.
The air here is cool.
This road is empty.
That class is easy.

grammarLessons.title: Yes-no questions with -ද
grammarLessons.explanation: A spoken statement can become a yes-no question by adding the question sound -ද.

examples.en: Are you coming today?
Is this correct?
Did you eat?
Are you leaving now?
Is this tea hot?
Is he or she coming tomorrow?
Are we staying here?
Is this yours?
Did they speak?

grammarLessons.title: Omitted subjects
grammarLessons.explanation: Speakers often omit I, you, or they when context already makes the subject clear.

examples.en: I am going home now.
I will come tomorrow.
I will stay here for a little while.
I am going to the shop now.
I am coming again tomorrow.
I will stay a little.
I will talk later.
I am working today.
I will read slowly.

grammarLessons.title: Noun descriptions without 'is'
grammarLessons.explanation: Spoken Sinhala often joins two noun ideas without a separate present-tense word for 'is'.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: He or she is a teacher.

examples.en: He or she is a teacher.
She is a doctor.
I am a student.
He is a teacher.
She is a nurse.
I am a student.
We are friends.
He or she is a driver.
You are a traveler.

grammarLessons.title: Plural nouns use several patterns
grammarLessons.explanation: Sinhala has several plural patterns rather than one universal ending, so learn frequent nouns together with their plurals.

examples.en: The children are at school.
There are books on the table.
People are waiting for the bus.

grammarLessons.title: Having with a dative possessor
grammarLessons.explanation: Spoken Sinhala often expresses have as something existing to a person. Use ඉන්නවා when the possessed referent is animate.

examples.en: I have a car.
He or she has a brother.
We have time today.

grammarLessons.title: Joining nouns with -යි ... -යි
grammarLessons.explanation: In speech, -යි can mark each item in a coordinated list. සහ is a more formal alternative for and.

grammarLessons.title: Direct requests and commands
grammarLessons.explanation: Short spoken commands often use a compact verb form; tone and politeness matter.

examples.en: Sit here.
Close the door.
Speak a little slowly.
Look here.
Bring the book.
Do not talk now.
Please hurry a little.
Do not forget that.
Go forward.

grammarLessons.title: Manner words before the action
grammarLessons.explanation: Words describing how an action happens, such as slowly or well, usually appear before the final verb.

examples.en: Please speak slowly.
He or she speaks Sinhala well.
The bus went quickly.

This cup is yours.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 7
courseLessons.focus: Core words and simple sentence order
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Build short present-tense sentences about common activities.

grammarLessons.title: Default subject-object-verb order
grammarLessons.explanation: A neutral Sinhala sentence normally places the main verb last.

examples.en: I read the book.
I drink tea.
She writes a letter.
I drink coffee.
We listen to songs.
You make food.
He or she opens the door.
She starts the class.
They hit the ball.

grammarLessons.title: Present and regular actions with -නවා
grammarLessons.explanation: The common colloquial -නවා form covers present, habitual, and contextually future actions.

examples.en: I study Sinhala every day.
He or she drinks coffee in the morning.
We play cricket on weekends.
I drink water in the morning.
You work on Saturdays.
He or she walks in the evening.
We listen to Sinhala every day.
She cooks twice a week.
They play after school.

grammarLessons.title: Omitted subjects
grammarLessons.explanation: Speakers often omit I, you, or they when context already makes the subject clear.

examples.en: I am going home now.
I will come tomorrow.
I will stay here for a little while.
I am going to the shop now.
I am coming again tomorrow.
I will stay a little.
I will talk later.
I am working today.
I will read slowly.

grammarLessons.title: Yes-no questions with -ද
grammarLessons.explanation: A spoken statement can become a yes-no question by adding the question sound -ද.

examples.en: Are you coming today?
Is this correct?
Did you eat?
Are you leaving now?
Is this tea hot?
Is he or she coming tomorrow?
Are we staying here?
Is this yours?
Did they speak?

grammarLessons.title: Wants and needs with ඕනේ
grammarLessons.explanation: The person who wants something often appears in the dative form.

examples.en: I want a tea.
I want a bottle of water.
We need two rooms.

grammarLessons.title: Alternatives with හරි ... හරි
grammarLessons.explanation: Repeating හරි after alternatives creates an everyday either-or choice.

examples.en: Have either tea or coffee.
Come either today or tomorrow.

examples.si: බස් එකෙන් හරි දුම්රියෙන් හරි යමු.
examples.en: Let us go either by bus or by train.

grammarLessons.title: Also and too with -ත්
grammarLessons.explanation: The particle -ත් adds the meaning also, too, or even to the item before it.

examples.en: I am coming tomorrow too.
He or she wants tea too.
We speak Sinhala too.

grammarLessons.title: Question words stay inside the sentence
grammarLessons.explanation: Words such as කවුද, මොකක්ද, කොහෙද, කවදාද, ඇයි, and කොහොමද normally remain where their answer would appear.

examples.en: Where are you going?
What are you eating?
When is he or she coming?
Who are you going with?
Where is he or she staying?
When are we leaving?
Why are you laughing?
How does this work?
Why did they come?

courseLessons.title: Lesson 12
courseLessons.focus: Core words and simple sentence order
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Practice pronouns with words and short useful phrases from your notes.

grammarLessons.title: Experiencers with මට, ඔයාට, and එයාට
grammarLessons.explanation: For wants, needs, ability, liking, feelings, and many bodily states, everyday Sinhala commonly marks the person with -ට. Do not automatically copy an English subject pronoun into Sinhala.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: I want or need to eat.

examples.en: I want or need to eat.
You can do this.
He or she needs help.
I like drinking hot tea.
Do you like listening to this song?
I am hungry today.
He or she feels cold.

grammarLessons.title: Recipients and destinations with -ට
grammarLessons.explanation: -ට can mark the person who receives something or the place someone moves toward. It does not make that word a direct object.

examples.en: I gave Mom a book.
I sent you a message.
I am going to the hospital.
He or she gave Mom a tea.
We are going to the shop.
I will show you the way.
He or she went home.

grammarLessons.title: Pronoun direct objects with -ව
grammarLessons.explanation: Use forms such as මාව, ඔයාව, and එයාව when a person is directly affected by an action. Keep them separate from dative forms such as මට and ඔයාට.

examples.en: He or she saw me.

grammarLessons.title: Adjective descriptions
grammarLessons.explanation: Many descriptions work as complete predicates without an extra copula.

examples.en: This food is tasty.
The weather is good today.
That room is big.
This tea is tasty.
Today is quiet.
That story is long.
The air here is cool.
This road is empty.
That class is easy.

grammarLessons.title: Yes-no questions with -ද
grammarLessons.explanation: A spoken statement can become a yes-no question by adding the question sound -ද.

examples.en: Are you coming today?
Is this correct?
Did you eat?
Are you leaving now?
Is this tea hot?
Is he or she coming tomorrow?
Are we staying here?
Is this yours?
Did they speak?

grammarLessons.title: Colloquial personal pronouns
grammarLessons.explanation: Everyday spoken Sinhala distinguishes singular and plural pronouns, while ඔබ is a more formal or respectful you.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 16
courseLessons.focus: Core words and simple sentence order
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Recognize core cardinal numbers and use them to count items.

grammarLessons.title: Numerals commonly follow the noun
grammarLessons.explanation: In a neutral quantity phrase, Sinhala commonly places the counted noun before its numeral.

examples.en: I have three books.
I bought two mangoes.
There are four chairs in the room.

grammarLessons.title: Indefinite singular nouns with -ක් / -ෙක්
grammarLessons.explanation: A singular noun meaning a or one commonly carries an indefinite ending. The exact form depends on the noun and whether it is animate.

examples.en: I have a book.
There is a dog outside.
She got a tea.

grammarLessons.title: Here, there, and over there
grammarLessons.explanation: මෙතන points near the speaker, එතන points to a known or addressee-side place, and අතන points farther away.

examples.en: The book is here.
You stay there.
The bus stop is over there.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 17
courseLessons.focus: Useful grammar, endings, and everyday meaning
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Ask the time and place an event on a day or at a time.

grammarLessons.title: Time and place before the verb
grammarLessons.explanation: Time and place information usually arrives before the final action.

examples.en: I am going home today.
We are going to school tomorrow.
He or she goes to the shop in the morning.
I am going to the shop today.
We are going to the beach tomorrow.
He or she is staying home tonight.
She goes to the office in the morning.
They go to the temple in the evening.
You are going to class now.

grammarLessons.title: Ordinal numbers before nouns
grammarLessons.explanation: Ordinal forms such as first and second normally come before the noun they rank.

examples.en: This is the first lesson.
He or she took the second bus.
Today is the third day.

grammarLessons.title: Dative -ට for to, for, and experiencers
grammarLessons.explanation: The -ට ending can mark a recipient, destination, or the person who feels, needs, or experiences something.

examples.en: I need water.
She feels cold.
We do not have time.
I need more time.
Do you understand?
She is afraid.
We are free today.
He or she is happy.
They need help.

grammarLessons.title: Possession with -ගේ
grammarLessons.explanation: Attach -ගේ to an animate owner or pronoun to express possession.

examples.en: This is Nadee's book.
That is my friend's car.
This is the child's bag.
This is our house.
That is your phone.
This book is the teacher's.
Her cup is on the table.
Their car is parked.
This bag is my friend's.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 19
courseLessons.focus: Useful grammar, endings, and everyday meaning
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Ask a price, understand a quantity, and request an item.

grammarLessons.title: Numerals commonly follow the noun
grammarLessons.explanation: In a neutral quantity phrase, Sinhala commonly places the counted noun before its numeral.

examples.en: I have three books.
I bought two mangoes.
There are four chairs in the room.

grammarLessons.title: Only with විතරයි
grammarLessons.explanation: විතරයි follows the limited item and means only or just that amount.

examples.en: I only have five minutes.
Only I am working today.
We only need to take these two.

grammarLessons.title: At least and even with -වත්
grammarLessons.explanation: Outside a negative expression, -වත් can set a minimum meaning at least or emphasize even.

examples.en: Try at least once.
Drink at least a little water.
Stay for at least ten minutes.

grammarLessons.title: From a place with -ින්
grammarLessons.explanation: The same family of endings commonly marks movement from a place.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: He or she left from home.

examples.en: He or she left from home.
I came from Colombo.
The bus left from Kandy.

grammarLessons.title: Together with using එක්ක
grammarLessons.explanation: Put එක්ක after a person or thing to mean with or together with.

examples.en: I went with my friend.
She spoke with Mother.
We played with the children.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 20
courseLessons.focus: Useful grammar, endings, and everyday meaning
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Ask where a place is and follow a short route.

grammarLessons.title: Dative -ට for to, for, and experiencers
grammarLessons.explanation: The -ට ending can mark a recipient, destination, or the person who feels, needs, or experiences something.

examples.en: I need water.
She feels cold.
We do not have time.
I need more time.
Do you understand?
She is afraid.
We are free today.
He or she is happy.
They need help.

grammarLessons.title: From a place with -ින්
grammarLessons.explanation: The same family of endings commonly marks movement from a place.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: He or she left from home.

examples.en: He or she left from home.
I came from Colombo.
The bus left from Kandy.

grammarLessons.title: Manner words before the action
grammarLessons.explanation: Words describing how an action happens, such as slowly or well, usually appear before the final verb.

examples.en: Please speak slowly.
He or she speaks Sinhala well.
The bus went quickly.

grammarLessons.title: Relational location words
grammarLessons.explanation: Sinhala places location words after the noun they relate to.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: There is a shop near the school.

examples.en: There is a shop near the school.
The cat is under the chair.
There is a garden behind the house.
The phone is on the table.
The shoes are by the door.
It is cool inside the house.

examples.si: කාර් එක පිටිපස්සේ බෑග් එක තියෙනවා.
examples.en: The bag is behind the car.
The dog is in front of the chair.
The books are under the window.

grammarLessons.title: Present and regular actions with -නවා
grammarLessons.explanation: The common colloquial -නවා form covers present, habitual, and contextually future actions.

examples.en: I study Sinhala every day.
He or she drinks coffee in the morning.
We play cricket on weekends.
I drink water in the morning.
You work on Saturdays.

grammarLessons.title: By or with using -න් / -ින්
grammarLessons.explanation: Instrumental forms can express the tool, means, or source involved in an event.

examples.en: I came by bus.
He or she wrote with a pencil.
We went to Kandy by train.

grammarLessons.title: Future meaning from time and context
grammarLessons.explanation: Colloquial Sinhala often uses a nonpast form with හෙට or another future time expression.

examples.en: I will come tomorrow.
We will go to Jaffna next week.
He or she will call tonight.
I will call tomorrow.
We will take a trip next month.
He or she will study tonight.
You will tell me later.
They have a meeting on Monday.
She will go home at the weekend.

grammarLessons.title: About with ගැන
grammarLessons.explanation: The postposition ගැන follows the topic and means about or concerning.

examples.en: We talked about the movie.

examples.si: මේ පොත ගැන ඔයා මොකද හිතන්නේ?
examples.en: What do you think about this book?
The teacher spoke about the exam.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 22
courseLessons.focus: Useful grammar, endings, and everyday meaning
courseLessons.referenceTopicTitle: මම, මට, මාව: everyday case roles
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Choose the natural pronoun form for a normal subject, a dative experiencer or target, and a direct object.

grammarLessons.title: Experiencers with මට, ඔයාට, and එයාට
grammarLessons.explanation: For wants, needs, ability, liking, feelings, and many bodily states, everyday Sinhala commonly marks the person with -ට. Do not automatically copy an English subject pronoun into Sinhala.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: I want or need to eat.

examples.en: I want or need to eat.
You can do this.
He or she needs help.
I like drinking hot tea.
Do you like listening to this song?
I am hungry today.
He or she feels cold.

grammarLessons.title: Recipients and destinations with -ට
grammarLessons.explanation: -ට can mark the person who receives something or the place someone moves toward. It does not make that word a direct object.

examples.en: I gave Mom a book.
I sent you a message.
I am going to the hospital.
He or she gave Mom a tea.
We are going to the shop.
I will show you the way.
He or she went home.

grammarLessons.title: Pronoun direct objects with -ව
grammarLessons.explanation: Use forms such as මාව, ඔයාව, and එයාව when a person is directly affected by an action. Keep them separate from dative forms such as මට and ඔයාට.

examples.en: He or she saw me.
I saw you.
We met him or her.
Did you see us?
He or she knows you.
I met Mom.
He or she caught the dog.

grammarLessons.title: Negative actions with නැහැ / නෑ
grammarLessons.explanation: The negative particle follows the verbal idea and often changes the verb to a focused form.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: I am not going to work today.

examples.en: I am not going to work today.
She does not eat meat.
We are not going out today.
I do not forget this.

examples.si: ඔයා අද බස් එක ගන්නේ නෑ.
examples.en: You are not taking the bus today.
He or she is not there.
We do not know about this.
She does not drink coffee at night.
They are not going to be late.

grammarLessons.title: Direct requests and commands
grammarLessons.explanation: Short spoken commands often use a compact verb form; tone and politeness matter.

examples.en: Sit here.
Close the door.
Speak a little slowly.
Look here.
Bring the book.
Do not talk now.
Please hurry a little.
Do not forget that.
Go forward.

grammarLessons.title: Feelings and bodily states with -ට
grammarLessons.explanation: Hunger, thirst, cold, sleepiness, and many feelings are framed as states experienced by someone.

examples.en: I am hungry.
She feels cold.
We are sleepy.

grammarLessons.title: Inability with බෑ
grammarLessons.explanation: බෑ expresses cannot, inability, or refusal in a compact spoken form.

examples.en: I cannot come today.
I cannot understand that.
We cannot stop now.

grammarLessons.title: Obligation and necessity
grammarLessons.explanation: Use ඕනේ for need or must and වෙනවා for something that has to happen.

examples.en: I have to go now.

examples.si: අපිට අද මේක ඉවර කරන්න වෙනවා.
examples.en: We have to finish this today.
She has to wake up early.

examples.si: මට අද මේක ඉවර කරන්න වෙනවා.
examples.en: I have to finish this today.
You have to leave very early.
He or she has to meet the doctor.
We have to bring the documents.
She has to call again.
They have to decide today.

grammarLessons.title: Having with a dative possessor
grammarLessons.explanation: Spoken Sinhala often expresses have as something existing to a person. Use ඉන්නවා when the possessed referent is animate.

examples.en: I have a car.
He or she has a brother.
We have time today.

grammarLessons.explanation: For wants, needs, ability, liking, feelings, and many bodily states, everyday Sinhala commonly marks the person with -ට. Do not automatically copy an English subject pronoun into Sinhala.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: I want or need to eat.

examples.en: I want or need to eat.
You can do this.
He or she needs help.

Do you like listening to this song?

He or she feels cold.

grammarLessons.title: Recipients and destinations with -ට
grammarLessons.explanation: -ට can mark the person who receives something or the place someone moves toward. It does not make that word a direct object.

examples.en: I gave Mom a book.
I sent you a message.
I am going to the hospital.
He or she gave Mom a tea.
We are going to the shop.
I will show you the way.
He or she went home.

grammarLessons.title: Pronoun direct objects with -ව
grammarLessons.explanation: Use forms such as මාව, ඔයාව, and එයාව when a person is directly affected by an action. Keep them separate from dative forms such as මට and ඔයාට.

examples.en: He or she saw me.
I saw you.
We met him or her.

grammarLessons.title: Present and regular actions with -නවා
grammarLessons.explanation: The common colloquial -නවා form covers present, habitual, and contextually future actions.

examples.en: I study Sinhala every day.
He or she drinks coffee in the morning.
We play cricket on weekends.
I drink water in the morning.
You work on Saturdays.
He or she walks in the evening.
We listen to Sinhala every day.
She cooks twice a week.
They play after school.

grammarLessons.title: Infinitives ending in -න්න
grammarLessons.explanation: The -න්න form expresses to do and combines with wants, ability, purpose, and other verbs.

examples.en: I want to speak Sinhala.
We need to leave early.
She went to the shop to buy the book.
I want to stay a little longer.
We need to understand this.
He or she went to the shop to buy bread.
She tried to fall asleep quickly.

grammarLessons.title: About with ගැන

courseLessons.title: Lesson 31
courseLessons.focus: Useful grammar, endings, and everyday meaning
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Study 20 Sinhala verbs, their main forms, and preserved romanized alternatives.

grammarLessons.title: Present and regular actions with -නවා
grammarLessons.explanation: The common colloquial -නවා form covers present, habitual, and contextually future actions.

examples.en: I study Sinhala every day.
He or she drinks coffee in the morning.
We play cricket on weekends.
I drink water in the morning.
You work on Saturdays.
He or she walks in the evening.
We listen to Sinhala every day.
She cooks twice a week.
They play after school.

grammarLessons.title: Completed past events
grammarLessons.pattern: past verb form at the end
grammarLessons.explanation: Past forms vary by verb, so learn frequent forms such as ගියා, ආවා, කළා, දැක්කා, and කිව්වා as whole units.

examples.en: We went to Colombo yesterday.
She made breakfast.
I spoke to him yesterday.
I woke up early this morning.
You read well yesterday.
He or she came by bus.
We ate dinner at night.
She wrote a letter to her friend.
They arrived on time.

grammarLessons.title: Infinitives ending in -න්න
grammarLessons.explanation: The -න්න form expresses to do and combines with wants, ability, purpose, and other verbs.

examples.en: I want to speak Sinhala.
We need to leave early.
She went to the shop to buy the book.
I want to stay a little longer.
We need to understand this.
He or she went to the shop to buy bread.
She tried to fall asleep quickly.

examples.si: ඔවුන් ගමන පටන් ගන්න ලෑස්ති වුණා.
examples.en: They got ready to start the trip.
Can you read this?

grammarLessons.title: Chaining actions with -ලා
grammarLessons.explanation: A -ලා participle connects a completed action to the next event.

examples.en: I ate and went home.
He or she opened the door and went inside.

examples.si: මම තේ හදලා වැඩ පටන් ගත්තා.
examples.en: I made tea and started work.
I washed my hands and ate.

examples.si: එයා බෑග් එක අරගෙන පිටත් වුණා.
examples.en: He or she took the bag and left.
We closed the door and slept.

examples.si: ඇය කවුළුව ඇරලා පිට බලලා හිටියා.
examples.en: She opened the window and looked outside.
They made tea and invited us.
Read this and tell me.

grammarLessons.title: Present and regular actions with -නවා
grammarLessons.explanation: The common colloquial -නවා form covers present, habitual, and contextually future actions.

examples.en: I study Sinhala every day.
He or she drinks coffee in the morning.
We play cricket on weekends.
I drink water in the morning.
You work on Saturdays.
He or she walks in the evening.
We listen to Sinhala every day.
She cooks twice a week.
They play after school.

examples.en: We went to Colombo yesterday.
She made breakfast.
I spoke to him yesterday.
I woke up early this morning.

We ate dinner at night.
She wrote a letter to her friend.
They arrived on time.

grammarLessons.title: Infinitives ending in -න්න
grammarLessons.explanation: The -න්න form expresses to do and combines with wants, ability, purpose, and other verbs.

examples.en: I want to speak Sinhala.

grammarLessons.title: Chaining actions with -ලා

grammarLessons.title: Chaining actions with -ලා

courseLessons.title: Lesson 35
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Explain why something happened and what will happen under a condition.

grammarLessons.title: Reasons with නිසා
grammarLessons.explanation: The reason normally comes first, followed by නිසා and then the result.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.en: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.si: රථවාහන තදබදය නිසා එයා පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: He or she was late because of traffic.

examples.si: විදුලිය නැති නිසා වැඩ නතර වුණා.
examples.en: The work stopped because there was no electricity.

examples.si: කාලය නැති නිසා අපි ඉක්මන් කළා.
examples.en: We hurried because there was no time.

examples.si: සද්දෙ වැඩි නිසා මට අහන්න බැරි වුණා.
examples.en: I could not hear because the noise was loud.

examples.si: අද සිසිල නිසා එයා ජැකට් එක ඇන්දා.
examples.en: He or she wore a jacket because it was cool today.

examples.si: වැඩ වැඩි නිසා ඇය පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: She was late because there was a lot of work.

examples.si: බස් නැති නිසා ඔවුන් ඇවිදගෙන ගියා.
examples.en: They walked because there was no bus.

examples.si: ඔයා කතා කළ නිසා මට තේරුණා.
examples.en: I understood because you explained it.

grammarLessons.title: Colloquial reasons with හින්දා
grammarLessons.explanation: හින්දා is a very common conversational way to introduce the cause of a result.
grammarLessons.exampleSi: මට වැඩ තිබුණ හින්දා එන්න බැරි වුණා.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: I could not come because I had work.

examples.si: මට වැඩ තිබුණ හින්දා එන්න බැරි වුණා.
examples.en: I could not come because I had work.

examples.si: වැස්ස වැඩි හින්දා අපි ඇතුළේ හිටියා.
examples.en: We stayed inside because it was raining heavily.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 39
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Study 20 Sinhala verbs, their main forms, and preserved romanized alternatives.

grammarLessons.title: Present and regular actions with -නවා
grammarLessons.explanation: The common colloquial -නවා form covers present, habitual, and contextually future actions.

examples.en: I study Sinhala every day.
He or she drinks coffee in the morning.
We play cricket on weekends.
I drink water in the morning.
You work on Saturdays.
He or she walks in the evening.
We listen to Sinhala every day.
She cooks twice a week.
They play after school.

grammarLessons.title: Completed past events
grammarLessons.pattern: past verb form at the end
grammarLessons.explanation: Past forms vary by verb, so learn frequent forms such as ගියා, ආවා, කළා, දැක්කා, and කිව්වා as whole units.

examples.en: We went to Colombo yesterday.
She made breakfast.
I spoke to him yesterday.
I woke up early this morning.
You read well yesterday.
He or she came by bus.
We ate dinner at night.
She wrote a letter to her friend.
They arrived on time.

grammarLessons.title: Infinitives ending in -න්න
grammarLessons.explanation: The -න්න form expresses to do and combines with wants, ability, purpose, and other verbs.

examples.en: I want to speak Sinhala.
We need to leave early.
She went to the shop to buy the book.
I want to stay a little longer.
We need to understand this.
He or she went to the shop to buy bread.
She tried to fall asleep quickly.

examples.en: They got ready to start the trip.
Can you read this?

grammarLessons.title: Chaining actions with -ලා
grammarLessons.explanation: A -ලා participle connects a completed action to the next event.

examples.en: I ate and went home.
He or she opened the door and went inside.

examples.si: මම තේ හදලා වැඩ පටන් ගත්තා.
examples.en: I made tea and started work.
I washed my hands and ate.

examples.si: එයා බෑග් එක අරගෙන පිටත් වුණා.
examples.en: He or she took the bag and left.
We closed the door and slept.

examples.si: ඇය කවුළුව ඇරලා පිට බලලා හිටියා.
examples.en: She opened the window and looked outside.

Read this and tell me.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 41
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Tell what happened and keep events in a clear order.

grammarLessons.title: Completed past events
grammarLessons.pattern: past verb form at the end
grammarLessons.explanation: Past forms vary by verb, so learn frequent forms such as ගියා, ආවා, කළා, දැක්කා, and කිව්වා as whole units.

examples.en: We went to Colombo yesterday.
She made breakfast.
I spoke to him yesterday.
I woke up early this morning.
You read well yesterday.
He or she came by bus.
We ate dinner at night.
She wrote a letter to her friend.
They arrived on time.

grammarLessons.title: Chaining actions with -ලා
grammarLessons.explanation: A -ලා participle connects a completed action to the next event.

He or she opened the door and went inside.

courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Explain why something happened and what will happen under a condition.

grammarLessons.title: Reasons with නිසා
grammarLessons.explanation: The reason normally comes first, followed by නිසා and then the result.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.en: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.si: රථවාහන තදබදය නිසා එයා පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: He or she was late because of traffic.

examples.si: විදුලිය නැති නිසා වැඩ නතර වුණා.
examples.en: The work stopped because there was no electricity.

examples.si: කාලය නැති නිසා අපි ඉක්මන් කළා.
examples.en: We hurried because there was no time.

examples.si: සද්දෙ වැඩි නිසා මට අහන්න බැරි වුණා.
examples.en: I could not hear because the noise was loud.

examples.si: අද සිසිල නිසා එයා ජැකට් එක ඇන්දා.
examples.en: He or she wore a jacket because it was cool today.

examples.si: වැඩ වැඩි නිසා ඇය පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: She was late because there was a lot of work.

examples.si: බස් නැති නිසා ඔවුන් ඇවිදගෙන ගියා.
examples.en: They walked because there was no bus.

examples.si: ඔයා කතා කළ නිසා මට තේරුණා.

grammarLessons.title: Reasons with නිසා
grammarLessons.explanation: The reason normally comes first, followed by නිසා and then the result.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 46
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Study 20 Sinhala verbs, their main forms, and preserved romanized alternatives.

grammarLessons.title: Present and regular actions with -නවා
grammarLessons.explanation: The common colloquial -නවා form covers present, habitual, and contextually future actions.

examples.en: I study Sinhala every day.
He or she drinks coffee in the morning.
We play cricket on weekends.
I drink water in the morning.
You work on Saturdays.
He or she walks in the evening.
We listen to Sinhala every day.
She cooks twice a week.
They play after school.

grammarLessons.title: Completed past events
grammarLessons.pattern: past verb form at the end
grammarLessons.explanation: Past forms vary by verb, so learn frequent forms such as ගියා, ආවා, කළා, දැක්කා, and කිව්වා as whole units.

examples.en: We went to Colombo yesterday.
She made breakfast.
I spoke to him yesterday.
I woke up early this morning.
You read well yesterday.
He or she came by bus.
We ate dinner at night.
She wrote a letter to her friend.
They arrived on time.

grammarLessons.title: Infinitives ending in -න්න
grammarLessons.explanation: The -න්න form expresses to do and combines with wants, ability, purpose, and other verbs.

examples.en: I want to speak Sinhala.
We need to leave early.
She went to the shop to buy the book.
I want to stay a little longer.
We need to understand this.
He or she went to the shop to buy bread.
She tried to fall asleep quickly.

examples.si: ඔවුන් ගමන පටන් ගන්න ලෑස්ති වුණා.
examples.en: They got ready to start the trip.
Can you read this?

grammarLessons.title: Chaining actions with -ලා
grammarLessons.explanation: A -ලා participle connects a completed action to the next event.

examples.en: I ate and went home.
He or she opened the door and went inside.

examples.si: මම තේ හදලා වැඩ පටන් ගත්තා.
examples.en: I made tea and started work.
I washed my hands and ate.

examples.si: එයා බෑග් එක අරගෙන පිටත් වුණා.
examples.en: He or she took the bag and left.
We closed the door and slept.

examples.si: ඇය කවුළුව ඇරලා පිට බලලා හිටියා.
examples.en: She opened the window and looked outside.
They made tea and invited us.
Read this and tell me.

grammarLessons.title: After an event with පස්සේ
grammarLessons.explanation: පස්සේ follows an event expression to place the main event afterward.

examples.en: We left after eating.

examples.si: වැඩ ඉවර වුණාට පස්සේ මම ගෙදර ගියා.
examples.en: I went home after the work finished.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 47
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Connect several ordinary actions into a short account.

grammarLessons.title: Chaining actions with -ලා
grammarLessons.explanation: A -ලා participle connects a completed action to the next event.

examples.en: I ate and went home.
He or she opened the door and went inside.

examples.si: මම තේ හදලා වැඩ පටන් ගත්තා.
examples.en: I made tea and started work.
I washed my hands and ate.

examples.si: එයා බෑග් එක අරගෙන පිටත් වුණා.
examples.en: He or she took the bag and left.
We closed the door and slept.

examples.si: ඇය කවුළුව ඇරලා පිට බලලා හිටියා.
examples.en: She opened the window and looked outside.

Read this and tell me.

grammarLessons.title: Before doing with කලින්
grammarLessons.explanation: Place කලින් after an infinitive to say before doing that action.

examples.en: Call me before you leave.

examples.si: වැඩ පටන් ගන්න කලින් මේක කියවන්න.
examples.en: Read this before starting the work.

grammarLessons.title: After an event with පස්සේ

grammarLessons.explanation: The construction -න ගමන් links an action continuing in the background with another action.

examples.en: We talked while walking along the road.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 49
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Explain why something happened and what will happen under a condition.

grammarLessons.title: Reasons with නිසා
grammarLessons.explanation: The reason normally comes first, followed by නිසා and then the result.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.en: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.si: රථවාහන තදබදය නිසා එයා පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: He or she was late because of traffic.

examples.si: විදුලිය නැති නිසා වැඩ නතර වුණා.
examples.en: The work stopped because there was no electricity.

examples.si: කාලය නැති නිසා අපි ඉක්මන් කළා.
examples.en: We hurried because there was no time.

examples.si: සද්දෙ වැඩි නිසා මට අහන්න බැරි වුණා.
examples.en: I could not hear because the noise was loud.

examples.si: අද සිසිල නිසා එයා ජැකට් එක ඇන්දා.
examples.en: He or she wore a jacket because it was cool today.

examples.si: වැඩ වැඩි නිසා ඇය පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: She was late because there was a lot of work.

examples.si: බස් නැති නිසා ඔවුන් ඇවිදගෙන ගියා.
examples.en: They walked because there was no bus.

examples.si: ඔයා කතා කළ නිසා මට තේරුණා.
examples.en: I understood because you explained it.

grammarLessons.title: Colloquial reasons with හින්දා
grammarLessons.explanation: හින්දා is a very common conversational way to introduce the cause of a result.
grammarLessons.exampleSi: මට වැඩ තිබුණ හින්දා එන්න බැරි වුණා.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: I could not come because I had work.

examples.si: මට වැඩ තිබුණ හින්දා එන්න බැරි වුණා.
examples.en: I could not come because I had work.

examples.si: වැස්ස වැඩි හින්දා අපි ඇතුළේ හිටියා.
examples.en: We stayed inside because it was raining heavily.

examples.si: මට සනීප නැති හින්දා වැඩට ගියේ නැහැ.
examples.en: I did not go to work because I was unwell.

grammarLessons.title: Compact conditions with -ොත්
grammarLessons.explanation: The suffixed -ොත් form creates a compact if-clause.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: If it rains, let us stay home.

examples.en: If it rains, let us stay home.
If you come, let us go together.
If he or she calls, tell me.

grammarLessons.title: Formal that-clauses with බව
grammarLessons.explanation: බව packages a fact as a noun-like clause, especially in formal speech and writing; colloquial speech often prefers කියලා.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: I know that he is coming.

examples.en: I know that he is coming.

examples.si: රැස්වීම අවලංගු කළ බව ඔවුන් දැනුම් දුන්නා.
examples.en: They announced that the meeting was canceled.
It appears that this information is correct.

grammarLessons.title: Trying an action with -ලා බලන්න
grammarLessons.explanation: After another verb, බලන්න can mean try doing it and see what happens.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: Try eating a little of this food.

examples.en: Try eating a little of this food.
Try saying this word.
Try writing it again.

grammarLessons.explanation: The reason normally comes first, followed by නිසා and then the result.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 53
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Study 20 Sinhala verbs, their main forms, and preserved romanized alternatives.

grammarLessons.title: Present and regular actions with -නවා
grammarLessons.explanation: The common colloquial -නවා form covers present, habitual, and contextually future actions.

examples.en: I study Sinhala every day.
He or she drinks coffee in the morning.
We play cricket on weekends.
I drink water in the morning.
You work on Saturdays.
He or she walks in the evening.
We listen to Sinhala every day.
She cooks twice a week.
They play after school.

grammarLessons.title: Completed past events
grammarLessons.pattern: past verb form at the end
grammarLessons.explanation: Past forms vary by verb, so learn frequent forms such as ගියා, ආවා, කළා, දැක්කා, and කිව්වා as whole units.

examples.en: We went to Colombo yesterday.
She made breakfast.
I spoke to him yesterday.
I woke up early this morning.
You read well yesterday.
He or she came by bus.
We ate dinner at night.
She wrote a letter to her friend.
They arrived on time.

grammarLessons.title: Infinitives ending in -න්න
grammarLessons.explanation: The -න්න form expresses to do and combines with wants, ability, purpose, and other verbs.

examples.en: I want to speak Sinhala.
We need to leave early.
She went to the shop to buy the book.
I want to stay a little longer.
We need to understand this.
He or she went to the shop to buy bread.
She tried to fall asleep quickly.

examples.si: ඔවුන් ගමන පටන් ගන්න ලෑස්ති වුණා.
examples.en: They got ready to start the trip.
Can you read this?

grammarLessons.title: Chaining actions with -ලා
grammarLessons.explanation: A -ලා participle connects a completed action to the next event.

examples.en: I ate and went home.
He or she opened the door and went inside.

examples.si: මම තේ හදලා වැඩ පටන් ගත්තා.
examples.en: I made tea and started work.
I washed my hands and ate.

examples.si: එයා බෑග් එක අරගෙන පිටත් වුණා.
examples.en: He or she took the bag and left.
We closed the door and slept.

examples.en: She opened the window and looked outside.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 55
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Tell what happened and keep events in a clear order.

grammarLessons.title: Completed past events
grammarLessons.pattern: past verb form at the end
grammarLessons.explanation: Past forms vary by verb, so learn frequent forms such as ගියා, ආවා, කළා, දැක්කා, and කිව්වා as whole units.

examples.en: We went to Colombo yesterday.
She made breakfast.
I spoke to him yesterday.
I woke up early this morning.
You read well yesterday.
He or she came by bus.
We ate dinner at night.
She wrote a letter to her friend.
They arrived on time.

grammarLessons.title: Chaining actions with -ලා
grammarLessons.explanation: A -ලා participle connects a completed action to the next event.

examples.en: I ate and went home.
He or she opened the door and went inside.

examples.si: මම තේ හදලා වැඩ පටන් ගත්තා.
examples.en: I made tea and started work.
I washed my hands and ate.

examples.si: එයා බෑග් එක අරගෙන පිටත් වුණා.
examples.en: He or she took the bag and left.
We closed the door and slept.

examples.si: ඇය කවුළුව ඇරලා පිට බලලා හිටියා.
examples.en: She opened the window and looked outside.
They made tea and invited us.
Read this and tell me.

grammarLessons.title: While or when with -ද්දී
grammarLessons.explanation: The spoken ending -ද්දී places one event during another event or situation.
grammarLessons.exampleSi: මම වැඩ කරද්දී එයා කතා කළා.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: He or she called while I was working.

examples.si: මම වැඩ කරද්දී එයා කතා කළා.
examples.en: He or she called while I was working.
He or she came while we were eating.
The children ran inside while it was raining.

grammarLessons.title: Clauses that describe nouns
grammarLessons.explanation: A verb-based description comes before the noun it modifies.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: The man who came yesterday is my friend.

examples.en: The man who came yesterday is my friend.
The book that is on the table is mine.
The film that we watched yesterday is good.

grammarLessons.title: Irregular participles in event chains
grammarLessons.explanation: Frequent verbs have common chained forms worth learning as chunks.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: He or she went to the shop and bought bread.

examples.en: He or she went to the shop and bought bread.
We went to the market and bought vegetables.
She went home and slept.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 56
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Explain why something happened and what will happen under a condition.

grammarLessons.title: Reasons with නිසා
grammarLessons.explanation: The reason normally comes first, followed by නිසා and then the result.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.en: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.si: රථවාහන තදබදය නිසා එයා පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: He or she was late because of traffic.

examples.si: විදුලිය නැති නිසා වැඩ නතර වුණා.
examples.en: The work stopped because there was no electricity.

examples.si: කාලය නැති නිසා අපි ඉක්මන් කළා.
examples.en: We hurried because there was no time.

examples.si: සද්දෙ වැඩි නිසා මට අහන්න බැරි වුණා.
examples.en: I could not hear because the noise was loud.

examples.si: අද සිසිල නිසා එයා ජැකට් එක ඇන්දා.
examples.en: He or she wore a jacket because it was cool today.

examples.si: වැඩ වැඩි නිසා ඇය පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: She was late because there was a lot of work.

examples.si: බස් නැති නිසා ඔවුන් ඇවිදගෙන ගියා.
examples.en: They walked because there was no bus.

examples.si: ඔයා කතා කළ නිසා මට තේරුණා.
examples.en: I understood because you explained it.

grammarLessons.title: Colloquial reasons with හින්දා
grammarLessons.explanation: හින්දා is a very common conversational way to introduce the cause of a result.
grammarLessons.exampleSi: මට වැඩ තිබුණ හින්දා එන්න බැරි වුණා.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: I could not come because I had work.

examples.si: මට වැඩ තිබුණ හින්දා එන්න බැරි වුණා.
examples.en: I could not come because I had work.

examples.si: වැස්ස වැඩි හින්දා අපි ඇතුළේ හිටියා.
examples.en: We stayed inside because it was raining heavily.

examples.si: මට සනීප නැති හින්දා වැඩට ගියේ නැහැ.
examples.en: I did not go to work because I was unwell.

grammarLessons.title: Compact conditions with -ොත්
grammarLessons.explanation: The suffixed -ොත් form creates a compact if-clause.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: If it rains, let us stay home.

examples.en: If it rains, let us stay home.
If you come, let us go together.
If he or she calls, tell me.

grammarLessons.title: Formal that-clauses with බව
grammarLessons.explanation: බව packages a fact as a noun-like clause, especially in formal speech and writing; colloquial speech often prefers කියලා.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: I know that he is coming.

examples.en: I know that he is coming.

examples.si: රැස්වීම අවලංගු කළ බව ඔවුන් දැනුම් දුන්නා.
examples.en: They announced that the meeting was canceled.
It appears that this information is correct.

grammarLessons.title: Speech and thought with කියලා
grammarLessons.explanation: කියලා packages words, thoughts, names, and propositions inside a larger sentence.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: He or she said that they are coming tomorrow.

examples.en: He or she said that they are coming tomorrow.
Mother said that the food is ready.

examples.si: මම ඒක හොඳ අදහසක් කියලා හිතනවා.
examples.en: I think that is a good idea.

examples.en: We informed them that we are coming tomorrow.

examples.si: ඇය ඔයාට කතා කරන්න කියලා මට කිව්වා.
examples.en: She told me to speak to you.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 60
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Study 20 Sinhala verbs, their main forms, and preserved romanized alternatives.

grammarLessons.title: Present and regular actions with -නවා
grammarLessons.explanation: The common colloquial -නවා form covers present, habitual, and contextually future actions.

examples.en: I study Sinhala every day.
He or she drinks coffee in the morning.
We play cricket on weekends.
I drink water in the morning.
You work on Saturdays.
He or she walks in the evening.
We listen to Sinhala every day.
She cooks twice a week.
They play after school.

grammarLessons.title: Completed past events
grammarLessons.pattern: past verb form at the end
grammarLessons.explanation: Past forms vary by verb, so learn frequent forms such as ගියා, ආවා, කළා, දැක්කා, and කිව්වා as whole units.

examples.en: We went to Colombo yesterday.
She made breakfast.
I spoke to him yesterday.
I woke up early this morning.
You read well yesterday.
He or she came by bus.
We ate dinner at night.
She wrote a letter to her friend.
They arrived on time.

grammarLessons.title: Infinitives ending in -න්න
grammarLessons.explanation: The -න්න form expresses to do and combines with wants, ability, purpose, and other verbs.

examples.en: I want to speak Sinhala.
We need to leave early.
She went to the shop to buy the book.
I want to stay a little longer.
We need to understand this.
He or she went to the shop to buy bread.
She tried to fall asleep quickly.

examples.si: ඔවුන් ගමන පටන් ගන්න ලෑස්ති වුණා.
examples.en: They got ready to start the trip.
Can you read this?

grammarLessons.title: Chaining actions with -ලා
grammarLessons.explanation: A -ලා participle connects a completed action to the next event.

examples.en: I ate and went home.
He or she opened the door and went inside.

examples.si: මම තේ හදලා වැඩ පටන් ගත්තා.
examples.en: I made tea and started work.
I washed my hands and ate.

examples.si: එයා බෑග් එක අරගෙන පිටත් වුණා.
examples.en: He or she took the bag and left.

examples.en: She opened the window and looked outside.

Read this and tell me.

grammarLessons.title: Until with කන්

examples.en: Stay here until I come.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 62
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Tell what happened and keep events in a clear order.

grammarLessons.title: Completed past events
grammarLessons.pattern: past verb form at the end
grammarLessons.explanation: Past forms vary by verb, so learn frequent forms such as ගියා, ආවා, කළා, දැක්කා, and කිව්වා as whole units.

examples.en: We went to Colombo yesterday.
She made breakfast.
I spoke to him yesterday.
I woke up early this morning.
You read well yesterday.
He or she came by bus.
We ate dinner at night.
She wrote a letter to her friend.
They arrived on time.

grammarLessons.title: Chaining actions with -ලා
grammarLessons.explanation: A -ලා participle connects a completed action to the next event.

examples.en: I ate and went home.
He or she opened the door and went inside.

examples.en: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.si: රථවාහන තදබදය නිසා එයා පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: He or she was late because of traffic.

examples.si: විදුලිය නැති නිසා වැඩ නතර වුණා.
examples.en: The work stopped because there was no electricity.

examples.si: කාලය නැති නිසා අපි ඉක්මන් කළා.
examples.en: We hurried because there was no time.

examples.si: සද්දෙ වැඩි නිසා මට අහන්න බැරි වුණා.
examples.en: I could not hear because the noise was loud.

examples.si: අද සිසිල නිසා එයා ජැකට් එක ඇන්දා.
examples.en: He or she wore a jacket because it was cool today.

examples.si: වැඩ වැඩි නිසා ඇය පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: She was late because there was a lot of work.

examples.si: බස් නැති නිසා ඔවුන් ඇවිදගෙන ගියා.
examples.en: They walked because there was no bus.

examples.si: ඔයා කතා කළ නිසා මට තේරුණා.
examples.en: I understood because you explained it.

grammarLessons.title: Colloquial reasons with හින්දා
grammarLessons.explanation: හින්දා is a very common conversational way to introduce the cause of a result.
grammarLessons.exampleSi: මට වැඩ තිබුණ හින්දා එන්න බැරි වුණා.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: I could not come because I had work.

examples.si: මට වැඩ තිබුණ හින්දා එන්න බැරි වුණා.
examples.en: I could not come because I had work.

examples.si: වැස්ස වැඩි හින්දා අපි ඇතුළේ හිටියා.
examples.en: We stayed inside because it was raining heavily.

examples.si: මට සනීප නැති හින්දා වැඩට ගියේ නැහැ.
examples.en: I did not go to work because I was unwell.

grammarLessons.title: Compact conditions with -ොත්
grammarLessons.explanation: The suffixed -ොත් form creates a compact if-clause.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: If it rains, let us stay home.

examples.en: If it rains, let us stay home.
If you come, let us go together.
If he or she calls, tell me.

grammarLessons.title: Formal that-clauses with බව
grammarLessons.explanation: බව packages a fact as a noun-like clause, especially in formal speech and writing; colloquial speech often prefers කියලා.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: I know that he is coming.

examples.en: I know that he is coming.

examples.en: They announced that the meeting was canceled.
It appears that this information is correct.

grammarLessons.title: Even if and although
grammarLessons.explanation: These forms concede one fact before giving a result that still holds.

examples.en: Although it rained, we went.
Although it was difficult, she tried.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 65
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Practice because,and,or,too with words and short useful phrases from your notes.

grammarLessons.title: Reasons with නිසා
grammarLessons.explanation: The reason normally comes first, followed by නිසා and then the result.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.en: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.si: රථවාහන තදබදය නිසා එයා පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: He or she was late because of traffic.

examples.si: විදුලිය නැති නිසා වැඩ නතර වුණා.
examples.en: The work stopped because there was no electricity.

examples.si: කාලය නැති නිසා අපි ඉක්මන් කළා.
examples.en: We hurried because there was no time.

examples.si: සද්දෙ වැඩි නිසා මට අහන්න බැරි වුණා.
examples.en: I could not hear because the noise was loud.

examples.si: අද සිසිල නිසා එයා ජැකට් එක ඇන්දා.
examples.en: He or she wore a jacket because it was cool today.

examples.si: වැඩ වැඩි නිසා ඇය පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: She was late because there was a lot of work.

examples.si: බස් නැති නිසා ඔවුන් ඇවිදගෙන ගියා.
examples.en: They walked because there was no bus.

examples.si: ඔයා කතා කළ නිසා මට තේරුණා.
examples.en: I understood because you explained it.

grammarLessons.title: Also and too with -ත්
grammarLessons.explanation: The particle -ත් adds the meaning also, too, or even to the item before it.

examples.en: I am coming tomorrow too.
He or she wants tea too.
We speak Sinhala too.

grammarLessons.title: Joining nouns with -යි ... -යි
grammarLessons.explanation: In speech, -යි can mark each item in a coordinated list. සහ is a more formal alternative for and.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: Mother and father are at home.

examples.en: Mother and father are at home.
There is both tea and coffee.
Nimal and Kamal are coming tomorrow.

grammarLessons.title: Before doing with කලින්
grammarLessons.explanation: Place කලින් after an infinitive to say before doing that action.

examples.en: Call me before you leave.
Wash your hands before eating.

examples.si: වැඩ පටන් ගන්න කලින් මේක කියවන්න.
examples.en: Read this before starting the work.

variationPool.explanation: Place කලින් after an infinitive to say before doing that action.

choices.en: Try eating a little of this food.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 70
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Explain why something happened and what will happen under a condition.

grammarLessons.title: Reasons with නිසා
grammarLessons.explanation: The reason normally comes first, followed by නිසා and then the result.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.en: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.si: රථවාහන තදබදය නිසා එයා පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: He or she was late because of traffic.

examples.si: විදුලිය නැති නිසා වැඩ නතර වුණා.
examples.en: The work stopped because there was no electricity.

examples.si: කාලය නැති නිසා අපි ඉක්මන් කළා.
examples.en: We hurried because there was no time.

examples.si: සද්දෙ වැඩි නිසා මට අහන්න බැරි වුණා.
examples.en: I could not hear because the noise was loud.

examples.si: අද සිසිල නිසා එයා ජැකට් එක ඇන්දා.
examples.en: He or she wore a jacket because it was cool today.

examples.si: වැඩ වැඩි නිසා ඇය පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: She was late because there was a lot of work.

examples.si: බස් නැති නිසා ඔවුන් ඇවිදගෙන ගියා.
examples.en: They walked because there was no bus.

examples.si: ඔයා කතා කළ නිසා මට තේරුණා.
examples.en: I understood because you explained it.

grammarLessons.title: Colloquial reasons with හින්දා
grammarLessons.explanation: හින්දා is a very common conversational way to introduce the cause of a result.
grammarLessons.exampleSi: මට වැඩ තිබුණ හින්දා එන්න බැරි වුණා.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: I could not come because I had work.

examples.si: මට වැඩ තිබුණ හින්දා එන්න බැරි වුණා.
examples.en: I could not come because I had work.

examples.si: වැස්ස වැඩි හින්දා අපි ඇතුළේ හිටියා.
examples.en: We stayed inside because it was raining heavily.

examples.si: මට සනීප නැති හින්දා වැඩට ගියේ නැහැ.
examples.en: I did not go to work because I was unwell.

grammarLessons.title: Compact conditions with -ොත්
grammarLessons.explanation: The suffixed -ොත් form creates a compact if-clause.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: If it rains, let us stay home.

examples.en: If it rains, let us stay home.
If you come, let us go together.
If he or she calls, tell me.

grammarLessons.title: Formal that-clauses with බව
grammarLessons.explanation: බව packages a fact as a noun-like clause, especially in formal speech and writing; colloquial speech often prefers කියලා.

examples.en: I ate and went home.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 77
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Explain why something happened and what will happen under a condition.

grammarLessons.title: Reasons with නිසා
grammarLessons.explanation: The reason normally comes first, followed by නිසා and then the result.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.en: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.si: රථවාහන තදබදය නිසා එයා පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: He or she was late because of traffic.

examples.si: විදුලිය නැති නිසා වැඩ නතර වුණා.
examples.en: The work stopped because there was no electricity.

examples.si: කාලය නැති නිසා අපි ඉක්මන් කළා.
examples.en: We hurried because there was no time.

examples.si: සද්දෙ වැඩි නිසා මට අහන්න බැරි වුණා.
examples.en: I could not hear because the noise was loud.

examples.si: අද සිසිල නිසා එයා ජැකට් එක ඇන්දා.
examples.en: He or she wore a jacket because it was cool today.

examples.si: වැඩ වැඩි නිසා ඇය පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: She was late because there was a lot of work.

examples.si: බස් නැති නිසා ඔවුන් ඇවිදගෙන ගියා.
examples.en: They walked because there was no bus.

examples.si: ඔයා කතා කළ නිසා මට තේරුණා.

grammarLessons.title: Reasons with නිසා
grammarLessons.explanation: The reason normally comes first, followed by නිසා and then the result.

grammarLessons.title: Completed past events
grammarLessons.pattern: past verb form at the end
grammarLessons.explanation: Past forms vary by verb, so learn frequent forms such as ගියා, ආවා, කළා, දැක්කා, and කිව්වා as whole units.

He or she came by bus.
We ate dinner at night.
She wrote a letter to her friend.
They arrived on time.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 84
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Explain why something happened and what will happen under a condition.

grammarLessons.title: Reasons with නිසා
grammarLessons.explanation: The reason normally comes first, followed by නිසා and then the result.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.en: Because of the rain, we did not go.

examples.si: රථවාහන තදබදය නිසා එයා පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: He or she was late because of traffic.

examples.si: විදුලිය නැති නිසා වැඩ නතර වුණා.
examples.en: The work stopped because there was no electricity.

examples.si: කාලය නැති නිසා අපි ඉක්මන් කළා.
examples.en: We hurried because there was no time.

examples.si: සද්දෙ වැඩි නිසා මට අහන්න බැරි වුණා.
examples.en: I could not hear because the noise was loud.

examples.si: අද සිසිල නිසා එයා ජැකට් එක ඇන්දා.
examples.en: He or she wore a jacket because it was cool today.

examples.si: වැඩ වැඩි නිසා ඇය පරක්කු වුණා.
examples.en: She was late because there was a lot of work.

examples.si: බස් නැති නිසා ඔවුන් ඇවිදගෙන ගියා.
examples.en: They walked because there was no bus.

examples.si: ඔයා කතා කළ නිසා මට තේරුණා.
examples.en: I understood because you explained it.

grammarLessons.title: Colloquial reasons with හින්දා
grammarLessons.explanation: හින්දා is a very common conversational way to introduce the cause of a result.
grammarLessons.exampleSi: මට වැඩ තිබුණ හින්දා එන්න බැරි වුණා.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: I could not come because I had work.

examples.si: මට වැඩ තිබුණ හින්දා එන්න බැරි වුණා.
examples.en: I could not come because I had work.

examples.si: වැස්ස වැඩි හින්දා අපි ඇතුළේ හිටියා.
examples.en: We stayed inside because it was raining heavily.

examples.si: මට සනීප නැති හින්දා වැඩට ගියේ නැහැ.
examples.en: I did not go to work because I was unwell.

grammarLessons.title: Compact conditions with -ොත්
grammarLessons.explanation: The suffixed -ොත් form creates a compact if-clause.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: If it rains, let us stay home.

examples.en: If it rains, let us stay home.
If you come, let us go together.
If he or she calls, tell me.

grammarLessons.title: Formal that-clauses with බව
grammarLessons.explanation: බව packages a fact as a noun-like clause, especially in formal speech and writing; colloquial speech often prefers කියලා.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: I know that he is coming.

examples.en: I know that he is coming.

examples.si: රැස්වීම අවලංගු කළ බව ඔවුන් දැනුම් දුන්නා.
examples.en: They announced that the meeting was canceled.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 85
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Invite someone, accept, decline politely, and settle a time.

grammarLessons.title: Let's with -මු
grammarLessons.explanation: The hortative ending invites the listener to do something together.

examples.en: Let us eat.
Let us go now.
Let us rest for a while.

grammarLessons.title: Polite requests with පුළුවන්ද
grammarLessons.explanation: Ask whether an action is possible to soften a request.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: Could you explain this a little?

examples.en: Could you explain this a little?
Could you open the window?
Could you tell me the way?
Could you give me a little water?
Could you say this word again?
Could you open the door a little?
Could you write this down for me?
Could you come quickly?
Could you explain that to me?

grammarLessons.title: Obligation and necessity
grammarLessons.explanation: Use ඕනේ for need or must and වෙනවා for something that has to happen.

examples.en: I have to go now.

examples.si: අපිට අද මේක ඉවර කරන්න වෙනවා.
examples.en: We have to finish this today.
She has to wake up early.

examples.si: මට අද මේක ඉවර කරන්න වෙනවා.
examples.en: I have to finish this today.
You have to leave very early.
He or she has to meet the doctor.
We have to bring the documents.
She has to call again.
They have to decide today.

grammarLessons.title: Alternatives with හරි ... හරි
grammarLessons.explanation: Repeating හරි after alternatives creates an everyday either-or choice.

examples.en: Have either tea or coffee.
Come either today or tomorrow.

examples.si: බස් එකෙන් හරි දුම්රියෙන් හරි යමු.
examples.en: Let us go either by bus or by train.

grammarLessons.title: Wants and needs with ඕනේ
grammarLessons.explanation: The person who wants something often appears in the dative form.

examples.en: I want a tea.
I want a bottle of water.
We need two rooms.

grammarLessons.title: Ability with පුළුවන්

grammarLessons.title: Polite requests with පුළුවන්ද
grammarLessons.explanation: Ask whether an action is possible to soften a request.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: Could you explain this a little?

examples.en: Could you explain this a little?
Could you open the window?
Could you tell me the way?
Could you give me a little water?
Could you say this word again?
Could you open the door a little?
Could you write this down for me?
Could you come quickly?
Could you explain that to me?

grammarLessons.title: Shared understanding with නේ
grammarLessons.explanation: Sentence-final නේ can invite agreement, remind the listener of shared knowledge, or mark a realization. Its force depends on intonation.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: It is really hot today, isn't it?

examples.en: It is really hot today, isn't it?
You know that, right.
This route is easy, isn't it?

grammarLessons.title: Managing a conversation with connectors
grammarLessons.explanation: These words continue, redirect, contrast, or advance a conversation.

examples.en: But I have another question.
So, what happened after that?
But I do not agree with that.

grammarLessons.title: Inability with බෑ
grammarLessons.explanation: බෑ expresses cannot, inability, or refusal in a compact spoken form.

examples.en: I cannot come today.
I cannot understand that.
We cannot stop now.

grammarLessons.title: Likes with කැමතියි and ආසයි

courseLessons.title: Lesson 87
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Give an opinion while distinguishing certainty, appearance, and hearsay.

grammarLessons.title: Probability and inference with ඇති
grammarLessons.explanation: Clause-final ඇති can present a conclusion as probable rather than certain.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: He or she is probably at home now.

examples.en: He or she is probably at home now.
The bus has probably been delayed.
They have probably already left.

grammarLessons.title: It seems or looks like with වගේ
grammarLessons.explanation: At the end of a situation description, වගේ marks an impression or appearance rather than a firm fact.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: It looks like it will rain today.

examples.en: It looks like it will rain today.
He or she seems tired.
This task seems difficult.

grammarLessons.title: Reported or hearsay information with ලු
grammarLessons.explanation: Sentence-final ලු signals that the speaker heard the information from someone else rather than asserting it directly.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: They say he or she is coming tomorrow.

examples.en: They say he or she is coming tomorrow.
They say the food at the new shop is good.
I heard that tomorrow is a holiday.

grammarLessons.title: Managing a conversation with connectors
grammarLessons.explanation: These words continue, redirect, contrast, or advance a conversation.

examples.en: But I have another question.
So, what happened after that?
But I do not agree with that.

grammarLessons.title: Polite requests with පුළුවන්ද
grammarLessons.explanation: Ask whether an action is possible to soften a request.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: Could you explain this a little?

examples.en: Could you explain this a little?
Could you open the window?
Could you tell me the way?
Could you give me a little water?
Could you say this word again?
Could you open the door a little?
Could you write this down for me?
Could you come quickly?
Could you explain that to me?

grammarLessons.title: Asking permission
grammarLessons.explanation: Permission questions often use a question ending or ask whether doing the action is possible.

examples.en: May I sit here?
May I come in?
May I look at this?

courseLessons.title: Lesson 89
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Study 20 Sinhala verbs, their main forms, and preserved romanized alternatives.

grammarLessons.title: Present and regular actions with -නවා
grammarLessons.explanation: The common colloquial -නවා form covers present, habitual, and contextually future actions.

examples.en: I study Sinhala every day.
He or she drinks coffee in the morning.
We play cricket on weekends.
I drink water in the morning.
You work on Saturdays.
He or she walks in the evening.
We listen to Sinhala every day.
She cooks twice a week.
They play after school.

grammarLessons.title: Completed past events
grammarLessons.pattern: past verb form at the end
grammarLessons.explanation: Past forms vary by verb, so learn frequent forms such as ගියා, ආවා, කළා, දැක්කා, and කිව්වා as whole units.

examples.en: We went to Colombo yesterday.
She made breakfast.
I spoke to him yesterday.
I woke up early this morning.
You read well yesterday.
He or she came by bus.
We ate dinner at night.
She wrote a letter to her friend.
They arrived on time.

grammarLessons.title: Infinitives ending in -න්න
grammarLessons.explanation: The -න්න form expresses to do and combines with wants, ability, purpose, and other verbs.

examples.en: I want to speak Sinhala.
We need to leave early.
She went to the shop to buy the book.
I want to stay a little longer.
We need to understand this.
He or she went to the shop to buy bread.
She tried to fall asleep quickly.

examples.en: They got ready to start the trip.
Can you read this?

grammarLessons.title: Chaining actions with -ලා
grammarLessons.explanation: A -ලා participle connects a completed action to the next event.

examples.en: I ate and went home.
He or she opened the door and went inside.

examples.si: මම තේ හදලා වැඩ පටන් ගත්තා.

I washed my hands and ate.

examples.si: එයා බෑග් එක අරගෙන පිටත් වුණා.

grammarLessons.title: Obligation and necessity
grammarLessons.explanation: Use ඕනේ for need or must and වෙනවා for something that has to happen.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 92
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Give an opinion while distinguishing certainty, appearance, and hearsay.

grammarLessons.title: Probability and inference with ඇති
grammarLessons.explanation: Clause-final ඇති can present a conclusion as probable rather than certain.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: He or she is probably at home now.

examples.en: He or she is probably at home now.
The bus has probably been delayed.
They have probably already left.

grammarLessons.title: It seems or looks like with වගේ
grammarLessons.explanation: At the end of a situation description, වගේ marks an impression or appearance rather than a firm fact.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: It looks like it will rain today.

examples.en: It looks like it will rain today.
He or she seems tired.
This task seems difficult.

grammarLessons.title: Reported or hearsay information with ලු
grammarLessons.explanation: Sentence-final ලු signals that the speaker heard the information from someone else rather than asserting it directly.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: They say he or she is coming tomorrow.

examples.en: They say he or she is coming tomorrow.
They say the food at the new shop is good.
I heard that tomorrow is a holiday.

grammarLessons.title: Managing a conversation with connectors
grammarLessons.explanation: These words continue, redirect, contrast, or advance a conversation.

examples.en: But I have another question.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 94
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Study 20 Sinhala verbs, their main forms, and preserved romanized alternatives.

grammarLessons.title: Present and regular actions with -නවා
grammarLessons.explanation: The common colloquial -නවා form covers present, habitual, and contextually future actions.

examples.en: I study Sinhala every day.
He or she drinks coffee in the morning.
We play cricket on weekends.
I drink water in the morning.
You work on Saturdays.
He or she walks in the evening.
We listen to Sinhala every day.
She cooks twice a week.
They play after school.

grammarLessons.title: Completed past events
grammarLessons.pattern: past verb form at the end
grammarLessons.explanation: Past forms vary by verb, so learn frequent forms such as ගියා, ආවා, කළා, දැක්කා, and කිව්වා as whole units.

examples.en: We went to Colombo yesterday.
She made breakfast.
I spoke to him yesterday.
I woke up early this morning.
You read well yesterday.
He or she came by bus.
We ate dinner at night.
She wrote a letter to her friend.
They arrived on time.

grammarLessons.title: Infinitives ending in -න්න
grammarLessons.explanation: The -න්න form expresses to do and combines with wants, ability, purpose, and other verbs.

examples.en: I want to speak Sinhala.
We need to leave early.
She went to the shop to buy the book.
I want to stay a little longer.
We need to understand this.
He or she went to the shop to buy bread.
She tried to fall asleep quickly.

examples.en: They got ready to start the trip.
Can you read this?

grammarLessons.title: Chaining actions with -ලා
grammarLessons.explanation: A -ලා participle connects a completed action to the next event.

examples.en: I ate and went home.
He or she opened the door and went inside.

examples.si: මම තේ හදලා වැඩ පටන් ගත්තා.

courseLessons.title: Lesson 95
courseLessons.referenceTopicGoal: Invite someone, accept, decline politely, and settle a time.

grammarLessons.title: Let's with -මු
grammarLessons.explanation: The hortative ending invites the listener to do something together.

examples.en: Let us eat.
Let us go now.
Let us rest for a while.

grammarLessons.title: Polite requests with පුළුවන්ද
grammarLessons.explanation: Ask whether an action is possible to soften a request.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: Could you explain this a little?

examples.en: Could you explain this a little?
Could you open the window?
Could you tell me the way?
Could you give me a little water?
Could you say this word again?
Could you open the door a little?
Could you write this down for me?
Could you come quickly?
Could you explain that to me?

grammarLessons.title: Obligation and necessity
grammarLessons.explanation: Use ඕනේ for need or must and වෙනවා for something that has to happen.

examples.en: I have to go now.

examples.si: අපිට අද මේක ඉවර කරන්න වෙනවා.
examples.en: We have to finish this today.
She has to wake up early.

examples.si: මට අද මේක ඉවර කරන්න වෙනවා.
examples.en: I have to finish this today.
You have to leave very early.
He or she has to meet the doctor.
We have to bring the documents.
She has to call again.
They have to decide today.

grammarLessons.title: Alternatives with හරි ... හරි
grammarLessons.explanation: Repeating හරි after alternatives creates an everyday either-or choice.

examples.en: Have either tea or coffee.
Come either today or tomorrow.

examples.si: බස් එකෙන් හරි දුම්රියෙන් හරි යමු.
examples.en: Let us go either by bus or by train.

grammarLessons.title: Only with විතරයි
grammarLessons.explanation: විතරයි follows the limited item and means only or just that amount.

examples.en: I only have five minutes.
Only I am working today.
We only need to take these two.

grammarLessons.title: Shared understanding with නේ
grammarLessons.explanation: Sentence-final නේ can invite agreement, remind the listener of shared knowledge, or mark a realization. Its force depends on intonation.
grammarLessons.exampleEn: It is really hot today, isn't it?

examples.en: It is really hot today, isn't it?
You know that, right.
This route is easy, isn't it?

grammarLessons.title: Managing a conversation with connectors
grammarLessons.explanation: These words continue, redirect, contrast, or advance a conversation.

But I do not agree with that.

grammarLessons.title: At least and even with -වත්
grammarLessons.explanation: Outside a negative expression, -වත් can set a minimum meaning at least or emphasize even.

Drink at least a little water.
Stay for at least ten minutes.
